reason: Moses is portrayed as an established national leader of the Israelite people in this passage. The text explicitly describes him as 'very great' (גָּדוֹל מְאֹד) in Egypt, and he holds a position of such prominence that Pharaoh's servants bow before him requesting his departure. Moses communicates God's commands directly to the people, and the text emphasizes that 'the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses,' demonstrating that his directives are followed as authoritative. Throughout this passage, Moses is actively leading the Israelites out of Egypt, organizing their exodus and giving them instructions they obey. While his authority is divinely ordained and he functions primarily as God's prophet rather than a secular leader, he is nonetheless functioning as a national leader directing his people.
